Question: What was a feudal army?
Old_Answer: A feudal army was an army in which the organization of the military was according to the feudal hierarchy of the society. That means that the ranking liege lord, would summon his vassals, who in turn would summon their vassals all the way down to the peasant bondsmen. The King of Denmark firetaxing (extorting) Visby after the Danish defeated the Swedish in 1361 It is often considered that a feudal army was an elite cavalry force surrounded by low quality infantry levies. However, that is not nessesarily the nature of feudalism, though it is partially true for some west European kingdoms. A king might call upon his duke, counts and barons, who personally will fight as elite mounted warriors. However the main stay of the army varies entirely on which companies the vassal choose to keep. The English famously maintained pretty skilled archers who were by no means low quality. The French were able to field almost entire armies of professional warriors and mercenaries. Other kingdoms called upon free cities to provide trained companies of engineers and crossbowmen such as Bercelona. The core of a feudal army then is simply that it is made up of vassal obligations, but what that army actually consists of in practice depended on regional specialties and effort put into maintaining their men at arms.
Answer_with_writing_sample: A feudal army was fundamentally a military force organized under the system of feudalism, which dominated medieval Europe from the 9th to about the 15th century. This system was characterized by the relationship between lords and vassals, where land was exchanged for military service. In essence, lords would grant parcels of land, known as fiefs, to vassals in exchange for loyalty and service, particularly in times of war. These vassals were typically knights, who were heavily armored cavalrymen trained for combat. The composition of a feudal army varied widely depending on the region and the specific context of warfare; however, it generally consisted of a core of professional knights supported by a retinue of foot soldiers, archers, and sometimes peasants. The army was often called upon in response to the feudal lord's direct orders, and the size of the force was contingent on the lord's resources, as each vassal was expected to bring a certain number of armed men based on the land they held. This decentralized approach to military organization meant that feudal armies were often not as cohesive or well-trained as modern military forces. Moreover, their effectiveness was subject to local loyalties and the personal ambitions of individual lords, which sometimes led to fragmented command structures and conflicts of interest during campaigns. Overall, a feudal army relied heavily on the social and economic fabric of feudal society, reflecting the intricate web of allegiances that defined the medieval landscape.

The feudal army was predominantly composed of knights who swore allegiance to their lords in exchange for land, known as fiefs. This led to varied levels of training and equipment among troops, depending on the wealth and resources of individual lords. Furthermore, the effectiveness of a feudal army was heavily influenced by the loyalty of its knights, making personal relationships and oaths of fealty crucial in warfare. Overall, while the feudal army played a critical role in medieval society and conflicts, it was both a reflection of the feudal system's complexities and a precursor to more organized military formations that would emerge in subsequent centuries

Question: Why is the M2 Browning still used currently? How good is it?
Old_Answer: M2 Browning, a 12.7mm heavy machine gun, is still in use essentially because no one has made a replacement for it yet. The M2 was originally introduced in 1933, which makes this gun over 90 years old. Indeed it appears that it might be replaced in the conceptional role by a Lapua Magnum 338, at least according to Garand Thumb who were looking at the newest version of the potential future machine gun. The Dshk is from 1938 and it was replaced by the NSV in 1971 inside the USSR. Additionally the 12.7mm Kord also is in use in Russia and affiliated countries. The Kord with a bipod weighs only 32 kg, and due to it’s recoil compensation can be fired with just that. The Kord has about the same rate of fire as the M2HB while the NSV has a higher rate of fire. If you really want more firepower, there are is also the KPVT, a 14.5mm machine gun, roughly 50% more powerful than a 12.7mm. The M2 is honestly an old bulky design, and the Americans are well aware of this, and have been for quite some time. It was supposed to be replaced in by the M85C in the 1980s, but it was deemed too unreliable. Then from 1990 they tried to replace it with the XM312, but it was cancelled in 2004, because it was too unreliable. Then from 2009 it was supposed to be replaced by the XM806 but it was cancelled in 2012 because it was delayed and complicated. XM806 In short, the US military has been trying to get rid of the M2HB for nearly 40 years, but the sheer incompetence of General Dynamics to create a new 12.7mm gun, has prevented this. Old_Answer: There are some things wrong with the Abrams tank, despite the endless optimism. Finally, the heavy tank is difficult to tow for other tanks, meaning only a few specialized recovery vehicles can do it. Well for example 500kg of TNT would produce an incident pressure of around 10 PSI at 100m from detonation site. While 1500kg of TNT would produce an incident pressure of around 18 PSI at 100m from the detonation site. 300% more TNT gives you just 80% more pressure at 100m. Pressure is what collapses buildings, and is the most notable effect of bombs on video. 500kg of TNT creates 18 psi at 70m. So by this logic, if we want to cover an area with 18 PSI blast waves of TNT. 3 bombs with 500kg of TNT could cover an area of 46,000m2 while 1 bomb with 1500kg could cover an area of just 31,000m2. So you can see despite being the same amount of bomb, the more but smaller bombs is actually better at destroying something by area. However, there is more to this, this is just the primary blast effect. We also have the secondary blast effect, we can call this kinetic penetration using delivery body, or we can call it shrapnel. The Bombs are encased in steel, the FAB-3000 has only 1400kg of explosive filler, the rest is steel. When the bomb explodes the steel casing tends to go flying with an initial velocity of about 2,300m/s if my calculations using HMX is right. This exponentially increases their ability to demolish, as well as almost guaranteeing termination of all life in the area, no matter what kind of cover is provided. No ODAB-3000 exists as far as I am aware. The Russian FOAB would probably be an ODAB-7000, at this scale the FOAB allegedly provides the power of 44t of TNT, which is twice as much as the Davy Crocket mini nuclear weapon.
